items.question: How much does a managed website cost?
items.answer: Plans start at $249/month for Lite and $449/month for Business, billed monthly in USD with no activation fee. Custom Solutions — e-commerce, bespoke software and advanced integrations — is scoped and quoted individually. See our Pricing page for the full comparison.

items.question: Is there a minimum commitment?
items.answer: No. Every plan is month-to-month with no long-term contract and no activation fee — cancel anytime.

items.question: Why is there no upfront website design fee?
items.answer: Instead of charging thousands upfront, we include the cost of designing, hosting, maintaining and supporting your website within one predictable monthly plan.

items.question: Is the free website preview really free?
items.answer: Yes. There is no payment or obligation to review your preview. If you like the direction, choose a plan and we'll work with you to complete and launch the website.

items.question: Who owns the website and domain?
items.answer: You always own your domain, and if you cancel before 6 months you receive all of your own content. After 6 consecutive months as a paying subscriber on any plan, the completed website is yours: if you leave after that, we provide your website files at no additional charge.

items.question: What if I need something updated?
items.answer: Lite includes 10 content updates a month and Business includes 20. Custom Solutions work is scoped and quoted individually rather than billed against a fixed monthly allowance. Requests beyond your monthly allowance, or larger than a normal update, are quoted separately, or you can move up a plan.

items.question: Can I cancel?
items.answer: Yes — every plan is month-to-month with no long-term contract, so you can cancel anytime. If you cancel before 6 months, you keep your domain and receive all of your own content. After 6 consecutive months as a paying subscriber on any plan, the completed website is yours and, if you leave, we provide your website files at no additional charge.

items.question: How long does it take to see my preview website?
items.answer: Timelines depend on your business and the information you provide. We confirm an expected timeframe when we look at your request.

items.question: Am I guaranteed a free preview?
items.answer: Not automatically. We look at every request first to make sure we can create something genuinely useful for your business before building a preview.

items.question: How many pages does each plan include?
items.answer: Lite includes up to 5 pages and Business up to 10. Blog posts, legal pages and thank-you pages don't count towards the limit. Custom Solutions — including e-commerce product listings — is scoped to your store or project rather than a fixed page count. Pages beyond your allowance are quoted separately, or you can move up a plan.

items.question: Can I add pages to my website later?
items.answer: Yes. Your plan includes a page allowance — up to 5 pages on Lite and 10 on Business — and you can add pages within it at no extra cost. Pages beyond your allowance are quoted separately, you can move up a plan, or for larger needs we scope a Custom Solutions project.

items.question: What counts as a content update?
items.answer: One update is a small change to text, an image or a section on your existing site, usually 20–30 minutes of work. Unused updates don't roll over to the next month. Full custom redesigns and new third-party integrations aren't updates; they are scoped and quoted separately.

items.question: Can I upgrade my plan later?
items.answer: Yes, at any time. We move your site to the new plan's features without rebuilding it from scratch or any downtime.

items.question: What does SynergyFirst Digital do?
items.answer: SynergyFirst Digital helps local businesses improve their online presence through website strategy, web design and development, local SEO, WordPress maintenance, digital marketing and practical automation solutions.

items.question: What types of businesses do you work with?
items.answer: We focus on local service businesses that depend on local customers, starting with garage door and tree service companies, and other trades such as roofing, plumbing, HVAC, electrical, fencing, concrete and remodeling.

items.question: Do you work with businesses outside India?
items.answer: Yes. We work remotely with businesses in the USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany and other European markets. Our process is designed for clear collaboration across locations and time zones.

items.question: Can you improve an existing website, or do you only build new ones?
items.answer: Both. We can audit and improve an existing website, rebuild an outdated one or create a new digital presence from the ground up. The right approach depends on what is currently limiting performance.

items.question: Do you provide support after the website goes live?
items.answer: Yes. We offer ongoing website care, maintenance and digital support based on what your business needs. You are not left alone after launch.

items.question: How do we get started?
items.answer: Book a free 20-minute call. We will discuss your business, current digital presence, immediate priorities and whether SynergyFirst Digital is the right fit for the work.

items.question: Should I book a call or request a free preview?
items.answer: Book a Free 20-Minute Call if you would like to talk through your goals with us directly. Request a Free Website Preview if you would rather see how your business could look first. If you are unsure, start with the call and we will point you to the right next step.

items.question: Does applying for a free preview guarantee I will get one?
items.answer: No. Submitting an application does not guarantee a preview. We review each application and follow up on the next steps.

items.question: Can you work with me if I am in another time zone?
items.answer: Yes. We work remotely with businesses across the USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Europe, and the booking tool lets you choose a time in your own time zone.

items.question: How should I prepare for the discovery call?
items.answer: Have your business name, your current website or Google Business Profile (if you have one) and the main problem you want solved to hand. The call is a conversation about fit and priorities, with no obligation.

items.question: What should a tree service company's website include?
items.answer: At minimum: a phone number that is one tap away on mobile, separate sections for tree removal, trimming and stump grinding, a clear service area, a short quote-request form, and space for photos of past work, reviews and credentials you can genuinely show. SynergyFirst Digital builds all of these into a managed website.

items.question: How do customers request a quote on a tree service website?
items.answer: Through a short quote-request form and a click-to-call button on every page. Most tree jobs are priced after a look at the site, so the form collects the details you need to plan a visit and sends each enquiry straight to you.

items.question: Can a tree service website handle storm and emergency calls?
items.answer: Yes. We give urgent jobs their own route, such as a prominent call button and a short request path, so a customer with a fallen tree knows what to do next. We do not publish response-time promises for your business unless you confirm them.

items.question: What should a garage door company's website include?
items.answer: At minimum: a phone number that is one tap away on mobile, separate sections for repair, new door installation and openers, a clear service area, a short quote-request form, and space for reviews, licences and project photos you can genuinely show. SynergyFirst Digital builds all of these into a managed website.

items.question: Can a garage door website handle urgent repair calls?
items.answer: Yes. Most garage door searches are urgent and made on a phone, so we keep click-to-call on every page and give emergency and scheduled jobs their own routes. We do not publish response-time promises for your business unless you confirm them.

items.question: Why should repair, installation and openers have separate pages?
items.answer: They are different jobs with different customers. A broken spring and a new door need different information, so separate sections let each visitor reach the job they need, with a call or quote request beside it.

items.question: What should a roofing company's website include?
items.answer: At minimum: a phone number that is one tap away on mobile, separate sections for roof repair, roof replacement and other exterior work, a clear service area, a short estimate-request form, and space for photos of completed work, reviews and credentials you can genuinely show. SynergyFirst Digital builds all of these into a managed website.

items.question: How do customers request an estimate on a roofing website?
items.answer: Through a short estimate-request form and a click-to-call button on every page. Most roofing jobs are priced after the roof has been looked at, so the form collects the details you need to plan a visit and sends each enquiry straight to you.

items.question: Can a roofing website handle storm-damage and leak calls?
items.answer: Yes. We give urgent jobs their own route, such as a prominent call button and a short request path, so a homeowner with a leak or storm damage knows what to do next. We do not publish response-time promises for your business unless you confirm them.

items.question: What trust information should a roofing website show?
items.answer: Anything you can genuinely show: licence and insurance details, accreditations you hold, warranty terms you offer, reviews and photos of completed work. We place them where customers look for reassurance, and we never invent them.

items.question: What should a plumbing, HVAC or electrical company's website include?
items.answer: At minimum: a phone number that is one tap away on mobile, separate sections for each trade you offer, a clear service area, a short service-request form, and space for photos of completed work, reviews and credentials you can genuinely show. SynergyFirst Digital builds all of these into a managed website.

items.question: Can a plumbing, HVAC or electrical website handle emergency calls?
items.answer: Yes. We give urgent jobs their own route, such as a prominent call button and a short request path, so a customer with a burst pipe, no heating or cooling, or a power problem knows what to do next. We do not publish response-time or 24/7 promises for your business unless you confirm them.

items.question: How do customers book a plumber, HVAC technician or electrician on the website?
items.answer: Through a click-to-call button on every page and a short service-request form where they describe the problem and the type of work. Each request goes straight to you, so you can call back or arrange the visit.

items.question: What trust information should a trade company's website show?
items.answer: Anything you can genuinely show: the licences and insurance you hold for each trade, accreditations, reviews and photos of completed work. Licensing rules differ by trade and location, so we show only what you confirm and never invent it.

items.question: What should a fencing, concrete or remodeling company's website include?
items.answer: At minimum: a phone number that is one tap away on mobile, separate sections for each type of work you offer, a clear service area, a short quote-request form, and a gallery of completed projects, reviews and credentials you can genuinely show. SynergyFirst Digital builds all of these into a managed website.

items.question: How should a fencing, concrete or remodeling website show past projects?
items.answer: With clear photos of completed work, grouped by type of project, and a short caption for each. These jobs are big decisions, so customers want to see finished results before they ask for a quote. We build the gallery and you supply the photos you have the right to use; we never use stock images as your work.

items.question: How do customers request a quote on a fencing, concrete or remodeling website?
items.answer: Through a short quote-request form and a click-to-call button on every page. Most of these jobs are priced after a visit to the site, so the form collects the details you need to plan it and sends each enquiry straight to you.

items.question: What trust information should a fencing, concrete or remodeling website show?
items.answer: Anything you can genuinely show: licence and insurance details where they apply, accreditations, warranty terms you offer, reviews and photos of completed projects. Requirements differ by trade and location, so we show only what you confirm and never invent it.
